summary.headline: Indigo Paints Q2 FY27 standalone EBITDA fell 33.8% to INR30.3 crore, margin 8.9% vs 15.3%, on high-cost inventory expensed through gross margin (38.5% vs 45.1%).
summary.overview: Standalone revenue rose 14.1% YoY to INR340.5 crore, but gross margin fell 660 bps to 38.5%, driving EBITDA down 33.8% and PAT to INR13.8 crore (4.0% margin). Management attributes the drop mainly to March-April raw material purchases at elevated prices being expensed in Q2, with a smaller contribution from unfavourable mix and higher discounts. H1 revenue grew 16.4% to INR690.5 crore, with H1 EBITDA up 3.2% and PAT up 8.3%. Management says the inventory pass-through ended by August and margins returned to near normal in September, and it expects gross margin recovery in Q3 and Q4.

segments.name: Paint categories (Q2 value / volume growth)
segments.commentary: Primers, distempers and others: +29.4% value, +9.4% volume. Enamels and wood coatings: +17.8% value, +8.2% volume. Emulsions: +13.3% value, +10.4% volume, with mix skewed to lower-end emulsions. Putty and cement paints: +12.6% value, -0.2% volume.

segments.name: Apple Chemie (subsidiary)
segments.commentary: Q2 revenue INR18.4 crore, +35.3% YoY; H1 revenue INR38.1 crore, +37.8%. Margins constrained by high raw material costs and slightly higher promotional spend.

guidance_outlook: Management expects gross margin to improve substantially from Q3 and to regain the industry-leading gross margin % in the seasonally strong Q3 and Q4.
EBITDA margins expected to normalise over Q3 and Q4; management does not expect a repeat of the Q2 profitability shock.

Management aims to grow 1.5x to 2x the industry; if industry grows about 15% it would be happy with 23-25%, and if industry growth falls to 5% it expects at least 10-12%. No firm numerical guidance given.
Management expects PAT for FY27 to be substantially higher in absolute terms than FY26, even with a marginal fall in EBITDA margin.
Industry has taken two price hikes in Q3 (one implemented 1 November, another due around 21 November); management says probably no further hike is needed at current raw material prices.
Management expects no substantive capex for the next two to three years; only minor capex of INR15-20 crore annually.
capex_capacity: New water-based plant at Jodhpur (90,000 kilolitres per annum) began trial production in September 2026; management expects full production from December 2026, with trials ending around end-November.
Jodhpur plant cost about INR275 crore; solar capacity 350 kW installed, with another 1,200 kW due by December 2026 (total over 1,500 kW).

Average capacity utilisation about 60%; peaks around 75% in October and March, troughs at 50-55%. Management sees capacity as non-constraining and says new capex is needed only when average utilisation exceeds 80%.

Network: 19,730 active dealers, over 12,700 tinting machines, 56 depots across 28 states, six manufacturing plants. New Bikaner depot opened; two to three more depots planned in Q3 and Q4. 19 Indigo Color Canvas stores.
demand_pricing: Industry raised prices by about 10-12% in response to the March-April raw material spike; a further hike of about 5% is in progress in Q3, giving roughly 16-17% cumulative.
Raw material prices fell in May-June, rose again in July-August; management says hedging is not available for these raw materials, so inventory management is the only tool.
October 2026 was a record sales month and the highest YoY monthly growth in three to four years, with a healthier product mix; management is cautious on November-December given Middle East risk.
Management says the industry leader's price moves dictate timing and magnitude for the industry; management expects volumes to remain resilient despite price hikes, citing low paint price elasticity.

Management says growth in waterproofing and lower-end emulsions is by choice, with higher influencer and sales-force spends rather than mainly discounts; higher discounts were a factor in the Q2 net revenue gap.

qa_highlights.question: Is Indigo's top-line growth in line with the industry, and what is the H2 growth outlook versus the 1.5-2x target?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the target is 1.5x to 2x the industry, not 2-3x. Q2 growth was in line with industry, possibly marginally ahead on the decorative part. It declined to give a number, citing geopolitical risk, but said October was strong.

qa_highlights.question: What is the gross margin bridge, and what will it take to restore sales and profit growth together?
qa_highlights.answer: Mix explains only about 2-2.5 points of the 650 bps decline; the rest is high-cost inventory expensed in Q2. Management expects FY27 PAT to be substantially higher in absolute terms than FY26.

qa_highlights.question: Will the water-based plant start commercial production, and could raw material shocks recur?
qa_highlights.answer: All permissions are in place. Management expects trials to end around end-November and full production from December. Management says the inventory effect has already been expensed and does not expect a recurrence, absent a renewed Middle East escalation.

qa_highlights.question: Will the two Q3 price hikes fully cover inflation, and has volume been affected?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said pricing is dictated by the industry leader and cover is uneven across products but roughly adequate overall. No volume impact seen so far; a further hike is probably not needed at current prices.

qa_highlights.question: Which segments and geographies are driving or losing growth, and is the slowdown temporary?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said metros are too small for Indigo to comment on. It cited disproportionate growth in waterproofing, lower-end emulsions and enamels, driven by voluntary spend, and saw no notable mix shift in urban, Tier 1, Tier 2 or rural areas.

qa_highlights.question: Are there capex plans, and what should be done with free cash flow?
qa_highlights.answer: No substantive capex for two to three years. Options for surplus cash are dividends, buybacks or M&A; management said a buyback would need to be substantial to matter and the Board will decide later.

risks_watch: Renewed Middle East escalation or crude above current USD 110-115 levels could again distort raw material costs and availability; management cannot predict this.
Whether the top-line initiatives (influencer spend, sales-force incentives, discounts) lift growth above industry in Q3 and Q4, since results are not yet visible.
Discount intensity and mix recovery; Q2 net revenue growth was 4.7 points below gross growth.
Whether Jodhpur water-based plant reaches full production by December as guided.
Consolidated and Apple Chemie margins, which were constrained by raw material costs and promotions.
Treasury income fell on adverse bond yield movements, a non-operating drag on Q2 PAT.
summary.management_tone: Candid and defensive on margins: management calls Q2 a difficult quarter and attributes it to identifiable inventory effects, then turns confident on Q3-Q4. On growth and guidance it is evasive, declining numerical targets and repeatedly saying it will "wait and see" for November-December.
key_quotes: Almost all of this decline is accounted for by a decline in gross margins, which was affected by an unfavorable product mix and mainly by high-cost raw material inventory carried over from the previous quarter.

The saving grace is that the pass-through of this higher-priced raw material inventory was largely over by August. And from September onwards, our gross margins and EBITDA margins are back to near normal.
We expect gross margins to improve substantially from Q3 onwards, and we expect to reclaim our leading position on gross margin percentage during the seasonally strong Q3 and Q4 quarters.
I do not share your pessimism that the overall PAT for the year is going to be similar to what it was last year.

adds.what: New water-based paint plant at Jodhpur, 90,000 kilolitres per annum (cost about INR275 crore)
Solar capacity: 350 kW installed, another 1,200 kW due by December 2026 (not productive paint capacity)

growth.why: No firm number; management aims for 1.5-2x industry growth, i.e. about 23-25% if industry grows 15% and at least 10-12% if industry grows 5%, with gross margin guided to recover substantially from Q3 as the inventory pass-through ended, backed by price hikes, record October sales and the Jodhpur plant (90,000 KL/yr, full production from December 2026).
